text:
Wooden butterfly

baking-soda smile

sawdust fly…

I like my belly

and the man at the liquor store

calls me

‘Mr. Schlutz.’

The racetrack cashiers

shout

‘THE POET KNOWS!’

when I cash my bets

the ladies

who get in and out of bed

say they love me

when I walk past them with

white wet feet.

Albatross with drunken eyes

Popeye’s dirty underwear

bedbugs of Paris,

I have saved the barricades

I have mastered

the automobile

the hangover

the tears

but I know

the final fate

like any schoolboy who watches

traffic crush

the cat as it passes.

My skull has a dent an

inch and a half long right at the

crown.

Most of my teeth are

in front,

I get dizzy in waves in supermarkets

I spit blood when I drink

whisky

and a sorrow comes over me

that grows into

pain

when I think of all the

good women I have known

who have dissolved

faded

into trivialities:

trips to Pasadena,

picnics with the children,

toothpaste caps

down the drain.

There is nothing to do

but drink

bet on the horses

bet on the poems

when the young girls

become women

and the machine guns

are aimed at me

crouched

behind walls thinner

than eyelids.

There is no defense

but all the mistakes

made.

Meanwhile

I shower

answer the telephone

make hard-boiled eggs

study movement and decay

and feel as good

as anyone

while I walk in the sun.

translation.title: Claws of Paradise
translation.editorial_note:
Translated from the supplied Spanish version attributed to Charles Bukowski. The surreal catalogue, capitalization, and supplied spacing are retained.

Imported as a translation without separate editorial review.
